title: White Gold Marine Services v. Pioneer Insurance
summary: The Supreme Court ruled that Protection and Indemnity (P&I) Clubs are engaged in insurance business and must comply with Philippine insurance regulations. A P&I Club provides marine insurance coverage against third-party claims and is thus subject to the Insurance Code.
doctrine: A Protection and Indemnity (P&I) Club is engaged in the insurance business within the meaning of the Insurance Code. Its operations in the Philippines require a license from the Insurance Commission. Any entity that assumes or distributes risk, whether or not for profit, is engaged in insurance business.
fullText:
CALLEJO, SR., J.:

The central issue is whether a Protection and Indemnity (P&I) Club is engaged in the insurance business in the Philippines and must obtain a license from the Insurance Commission.

Section 2(2) of the Insurance Code defines insurance as a contract whereby one undertakes for a consideration to indemnify another against loss, damage or liability arising from an unknown or contingent event. A P&I Club functions essentially as an insurer providing marine insurance coverage.

The test to determine if a contract is an insurance contract is whether the assumption of risk and indemnification of loss are its principal object and purpose. The P&I Club's undertaking to indemnify its members against third-party claims falls squarely within the definition of insurance.
